property_summary: After initializing the contract and depositing 100 wei, then calling Collect(100) with MinSum=0, reference contract allows the collect and reduces balance to 0, while bug reverts because SetMinSum was not callable before initialization so MinSum remained 0 and the collect succeeds; actually, both succeed. The real difference is that after initialization and a successful SetMinSum(100), the reference SetMinSum can be called again (reverting because intitalized), while the buggy SetMinSum reverts when intitalized is false, so it can only be set once after initialization. The concrete witness: caller deposits 1 wei, then SetMinSum is set to 0 (before initialization), then Initialized is called, then Collect(0) is called — both succeed with same state. Choosing MinSum=1, caller deposits 1 wei, then SetMinSum(0) before init, then Init, then Collect(1) — in reference, MinSum is 0 so Collect(1) succeeds; in bug, SetMinSum reverts because !intitalized, so MinSum stays default 0, Collect(1) also succeeds. The difference actually appears when we try to call SetMinSum after init: reference reverts, buggy allows. So scenario: set MinSum=0 before init, init, then call SetMinSum(0) after init — reference reverts, buggy does not. But the observation point is: after init, call SetMinSum(1) — reference reverts (ok=false), buggy sets MinSum=1 (ok=true). Then assertion: after that, c.MinSum() differs. So the property: SetMinSum reverts when called after initialization (reference holds, bug violates).
change_summary: Replace the revert condition with different check that sets MinSum only when intitalized is true, making SetMinSum revert when not initialized.
